description: The Mendeley Heritage_cracks release holds high-resolution photographs of superficial cracking on ignimbrite masonry and lime-based plaster in heritage buildings in Morelia, Mexico. The article distinguishes 686 smartphone images from streets and architectural elements from 1,030 augmented images, for a total of 1,716. The public version 3 lists one ZIP archive under CC BY 4.0 and the repository describes training, validation and test partitions. These images can help test a visual condition-monitoring model for heritage assets, but a visible crack label does not establish structural capacity or a rate of deterioration. One city, material type, camera viewpoint and possible correlation between originals and augmentations are limitations when estimating model performance in other sites. A reviewer-assessed use is comparing surface-damage indicators before assigning inspection priorities. data-rescult-european-interoperable-database-cultural-heritage is a related heritage resource but has different scope; no building-level crosswalk was tested. No image archive was downloaded.
